hints.title: Unique Element Placement Invariant
hints.text: Unlike subsets where ordering does not matter, a permutation must include all elements in every possible order. How can you ensure each number appears exactly once in each candidate sequence?

hints.title: Unused Element Selection
hints.text: At each step of constructing a sequence of length N, pick any element that has not yet been selected in the current path.

hints.title: State Restoration Permutation Procedure
hints.text: Define a recursive helper that maintains the current path and a set or boolean array of used elements. If the path length equals the array length, append a copy of path to results. Otherwise, iterate through all elements: if an element is unused, mark it used, append to path, recurse, then unmark it and pop from path.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of nums array (1 <= N <= 6)
complexity.notes: Produces exactly N! permutations of length N with O(N) recursion stack.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating random shuffles or checking all N^N sequences and filtering takes O(N^N) time, which is vastly slower than N! exploration.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Tracking used elements in a boolean array or set explores only the exact N! valid permutations in O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Explicit state restoration (push/pop and visited toggle), deep-copying paths when appending to results, understanding the N! factorial complexity.
